title: Polylogarithmic tree-independence conjecture for induced-minor-free graphs
exact_utf8_statement:
For a positive integer $t$, let $K_{t,t}$ be the complete bipartite graph, and let $W_{t\times t}$ be the $t\times t$-wall. An **induced minor** is a graph obtained by taking an induced subgraph and contracting pairwise vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs. The tree independence number is the minimum, over all tree decompositions, of the maximum independence number of a bag.

**Polylogarithmic tree-independence conjecture.** For every positive integer $t$, there is an integer $d=d(t)$ such that for every $n\ge2$, every $n$-vertex graph with no induced minor isomorphic to $K_{t,t}$ or to $W_{t\times t}$ has tree independence number at most $\log^d n$.

This is presented as a further goal toward understanding induced-minor obstructions to polylogarithmic tree independence. The source describes the preceding conjecture and the methods developed there as promising steps, but gives no resolution.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every t exists d(t), all n>=2 and both induced-minor exclusions.
individual_disposition: Polylogarithmic bag-independence bound requires structural decomposition at every order; no small obstruction or uniform construction obtained. PARK_DEEP.

title: The Scarf resolution conjecture for powers of extremal ideals
exact_utf8_statement:
For an integer $q\geq 1$, let $\mathcal{S}_q=\mathsf{k}[x_A\colon \emptyset\neq A\subseteq [q]]$, and let $\mathcal{E}_q$ be the ideal generated by

$$
\epsilon_i=\prod_{i\in A\subseteq [q]}x_A\qquad (i\in[q]).
$$

For $r\geq 1$, write $\mathcal{E}_q^r=(\mathcal{E}_q)^r$ and let $\mathbb{S}(\mathcal{E}_q^r)$ denote its Scarf simplicial complex. **The Scarf resolution conjecture.** For all integers $r,q\geq 1$, $\mathbb{S}(\mathcal{E}_q^r)$ supports a minimal free resolution of $\mathcal{E}_q^r$.

A Scarf resolution is the smallest possible cellular resolution in this setting, and would give an explicit minimal free resolution for every power of every extremal ideal. The conjecture was previously speculated in the cited work and is presented here as a guiding conjecture supported by the paper's additional evidence and results.
quantifiers_and_scope: All q,r>=1 and a coefficient field k; full minimal resolution, not selected Betti numbers.
individual_disposition: Would need acyclicity in every multigraded strand of the Scarf complex; finite powers cannot certify all q,r. PARK_DEEP.

title: General conjecture on general-position subsets of finite affine spaces
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $d53d_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements, and let $d53d_q^d$ be its $d$-dimensional affine space. For a $p$-random subset of $d53d_q^d$, let $d6fc(d53d_q^d,p)$ denote the maximum size of a point set in general position, meaning that no $d+1$ points lie in a $(d-1)$-dimensional affine subspace. Here $p$ is the independent probability with which each point is selected.

**General conjecture.** For every integer $d d45a 2$, there is a positive real number $C=C(d)$ such that, as the prime power $q$ tends to infinity, with high probability,

$$
\alpha(\mathbb{F}_q^{d},p)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}\Theta(pq^d)&\textrm{ for }\quad \omega(q^{-d})=p=o(q^{-d+1/d}),\\Theta(pq)&\textrm{ for }\quad Cq^{-1+1/d}\log^2q\leqslant p\leqslant1,
\end{array}\right.
$$

and

$$
\Omega(q^{1/d}/\log q)=\alpha(\mathbb{F}_q^{d},p)=O(q^{1/d}\log^2q)
$$

for $q^{-d+1/d}/\log q\leqslant p<Cq^{-1+1/d}\log^2q$, where all implicit constants depend only on $d$. This conjecture predicts the order of magnitude of the largest general-position subset across all relevant ranges of the sampling probability; the paper establishes the three-dimensional case up to polylogarithmic factors, while the general statement remains open.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every dimension d and all prime-power q with three p ranges, asymptotically with high probability.
individual_disposition: Literal d inequality and piecewise Theta formula are corrupted (d45a and missing row separator). No complete-statement coverage; restoring characters is not a result. HOLD_TRANSCRIPTION.

title: The Browkin–Brzeziński strong $n$-conjecture for subsum-free integer tuples
exact_utf8_statement:
For a non-zero integer $m$, let $\operatorname{rad}(m)$ be its largest square-free positive divisor. For $n\geq 3$ and $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ with all $a_i\neq 0$, define

$$
q(a)=\frac{\log(\max(|a_1|,\ldots,|a_n|))}{\log\operatorname{rad}(a_1\cdots a_n)}.
$$

For a sequence $A=\{a^{(1)},a^{(2)},\ldots\}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^n$, define

$$
Q_A=\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}q(a^{(k)}).
$$

Let $A(n)\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^n$ be the set of $n$-tuples satisfying (Z) $a_1+\cdots+a_n=0$, (S1) no nontrivial subsum with coefficients in $\{0,1\}$ vanishes, and (G1) $\operatorname{gcd}(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=1$. **The Browkin–Brzeziński $n$-conjecture.** For every $n\geq 3$, one has

$$
Q_{A(n)}=2n-5.
$$

This is one of the strong $n$-conjectures studied over the rational integers; the supplied material does not state whether it has been resolved.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every n>=3, limsup over A(n), including the n=3 abc-scale case.
individual_disposition: Q_A is introduced for sequences but A(n) is a set without an exhaustion convention; full intended Diophantine assertion remains deep even after repair. HOLD_SCOPE.

title: Mean-field approximation conjecture for upper tails of strictly balanced subgraph counts
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $H$ be a strictly balanced graph, with $v_H$ vertices, $e_H$ edges, maximum degree $\Delta$, and parameter $\alpha_H^*$. Let $\Psi_{p,H}(\delta)$ denote the mean-field variational problem for the upper tail of the number $N(H,\mathbb{G}(n,p))$ of copies of $H$ in the Erdős–Rényi random graph. **Mean-field approximation conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, $\delta>0$, and $p$ satisfying

$$
p\ll n^{-1/\Delta},\qquad n^{v_H}p^{e_H}\gg (\log n)^{\alpha_H^*/(\alpha_H^*-1)},
$$

for all sufficiently large $n$,

$$
(1-\varepsilon)\Psi_{p,H}\left(\delta(1-\varepsilon)\right)\leqslant -\log\mathbb{P}\left(N(H,\mathbb{G}(n,p))\geqslant(1+\delta)n^{v_H}p^{e_H}\right)\leqslant(1+\varepsilon)\Psi_{p,H}\left(\delta(1+\varepsilon)\right).
$$

The theorem immediately preceding this conjecture establishes the analogous mean-field approximation for stars $H=K_{1,r}$ in a different sparsity regime. The conjecture proposes that the same approximation holds for every strictly balanced graph in the stated regime, extending the known result for irregular subgraph counts and identifying the variational problem as the correct logarithmic upper-tail scale.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every strictly balanced H, epsilon in (0,1), delta>0 and p(n) in both asymptotic regimes.
individual_disposition: alpha_H^* and the variational functional Psi are not defined; requires exponential upper-tail comparison, not a star instance. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Mean-regime conjecture for the maximum and extremal process of two-speed branching random walk
exact_utf8_statement:
Suppose that $\mathcal{L}_1$ and $\mathcal{L}_2$ are non-lattice. Assume that there exist $theta_1^*,theta_2^*>0$ such that $\mathcal{L}_1$ and $\mathcal{L}_2$ satisfy assumptions (6), (7), and (8), with $theta_1^*=theta_2^*$. Let $theta:=theta_1^*$ and

$$
m_n:=\kappa_1'(\theta)\lfloor tn\rfloor+\kappa_2'(\theta)(n-\lfloor tn\rfloor)-\frac{3}{2\theta}\log n.
$$

**Mean-regime conjecture.** There exists a constant $C_{\mathrm{m}}>0$ such that, for every $y\in\mathbb{R}$,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{P}(M_n^{(n)}-m_n\leq y)=\mathbb{E}\left(e^{-C_{\mathrm{m}}Z^{(1)}e^{-\theta y}}\right),
$$

and the extremal process

$$
\mathcal{E}_n:=\sum_{|u|=n}\delta_{V^{(n)}(u)-m_n}
$$

converges in law to a randomly shifted decorated Poisson point process $\mathcal{E}$ with random intensity measure $C_{\mathrm{m}}Z^{(1)}\theta e^{-\theta y}dy$ and decoration $\mathcal{D}^{(2)}$. Here $\mathcal{D}^{(2)}$ is the limit in law of

$$
\sum_{|u|=n}\delta_{V_2(u)-\max_{|u|=n}V_2(u)}
$$

conditioned on $\{\max_{|u|=n}V_2(u)\geq\kappa_2'(\theta)n\}$. The conjecture concerns the as-yet unstudied mean regime for branching Brownian motion; it predicts both the limiting law of the centered maximum and the limiting extremal process.
quantifiers_and_scope: Equal positive critical theta values and every y, plus extremal-process convergence.
individual_disposition: Assumptions (6)-(8), kappa, derivative martingale and two-speed law are external; no full theorem target can be certified from literal text. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Girã o, Snyder, and Popielarz's linear minimum out-degree conjecture for linked tournaments
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $k$ be an integer. A **tournament** is a digraph obtained by orienting each edge of a complete graph in exactly one direction, and a tournament is **$r$-connected** when deletion of any set of at most $r-1$ vertices leaves a strongly connected digraph. A digraph is **$k$-linked** if, for every $2k$ distinct vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_k,y_1,\ldots,y_k$, it contains pairwise vertex-disjoint paths from $x_i$ to $y_i$ for all $i\in[k]$. The minimum out-degree is the minimum out-degree among its vertices.

**Girã o, Snyder, and Popielarz's conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>0$ such that every $(2k+1)$-connected tournament with minimum out-degree at least $Ck$ is $k$-linked.

This conjecture asks whether the connectivity bound in the cited theorem can be reduced to $2k+1$ while retaining a linear minimum out-degree condition. The supplied text gives no evidence that it has been resolved.
quantifiers_and_scope: One universal C for every positive k and every (2k+1)-connected tournament of minimum outdegree Ck.
individual_disposition: A single k-linkage construction must control all terminal choices; fixed k or high connectivity is insufficient. PARK_DEEP.

title: Stein's dimension-free maximal inequality conjecture for convex symmetric bodies
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $d\in\mathbb{Z}_+$, let $\mathfrak B(d)$ be the set of all convex symmetric bodies in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and for $U\in\mathfrak B(d)$ let $\mathcal C(p,\mathbb{R}_+,U)$ be the smallest constant in the discrete maximal inequality

$$
\left\|\sup_{t>0}|\mathcal M_t^U f|\right\|_{\ell^p(\mathbb{Z}^d)}\leq \mathcal C(p,\mathbb{R}_+,U)\|f\|_{\ell^p(\mathbb{Z}^d)}.
$$

**Stein's conjecture.** For every $p\in(1,\infty]$ there is a constant $C_p>0$ such that

$$
\sup_{d\in\mathbb{Z}_+}\sup_{U\in\mathfrak B(d)}\mathcal C(p,\mathbb{R}_+,U)\leq C_p.
$$

This asks for dimension-free bounds for discrete maximal operators associated with convex symmetric bodies. The corresponding bound is finite in each fixed dimension for every $p\in(1,\infty]$, but uniformity over all dimensions and all convex symmetric bodies remains a major open problem arising from Stein's work.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every p>1 with a constant uniform over dimension and every symmetric convex body.
individual_disposition: Discrete averaging operator M_t^U is not specified; replacing by continuous averaging would change the problem. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Holroyd–Talbot–Borg conjecture for intersecting faces of simplicial complexes
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $\Delta$ be a simplicial complex whose smallest facet has $d$ vertices. For a vertex $v$ of $\Delta$, let $\operatorname{link}_{\Delta}v$ denote its link, and let $f_{r-1}(\operatorname{link}_{\Delta}v)$ be the number of faces of dimension $r-1$ in that link. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a family of pairwise-intersecting faces of $\Delta$, each with $r$ elements.

**Holroyd–Talbot–Borg conjecture.** If $r\leq d/2$, then there is some vertex $v$ of $\Delta$ such that

$$
|\mathcal{A}|\leq f_{r-1}(\operatorname{link}_{\Delta}v).
$$

If equality holds and $r<d/2$, then $\mathcal{A}$ consists of the $r$-element faces containing some vertex $v$.

This extends Erdős–Ko–Rado-type results from uniform set systems and independence complexes of graphs to arbitrary simplicial complexes. The source presents it as the question raised by Holroyd and Talbot and extended by Borg; its resolution is not specified here.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every complex of minimum facet size d, r<=d/2, with a rigidity claim when r<d/2.
individual_disposition: Link faces of dimension r-1 correspond to stars of size r+1, whereas the family has size r faces. Indexing/source fidelity must be resolved before any purported EKR adaptation. HOLD_SCOPE.

title: Small tree-foliation conjecture for positively curved Riemannian 3-spheres
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $(S^3,g)$ be a Riemannian 3-sphere with scalar curvature $R_g\geq \Lambda_0>0$. A **tree-foliation** $\{\Sigma_t\}_{t\in T}$ is a foliation of $(S^3,g)$ by surfaces whose parameter space has the structure of a tree. For a leaf $\Sigma_t$, let

$$
\operatorname{diam}(\Sigma_t)=\sup_{x,y\in\Sigma_t}\{\operatorname{dist}_{\Sigma_t}(x,y)\}
$$

denote its intrinsic diameter. **Small tree-foliation conjecture.** There exists a constant $C>0$ such that $(S^3,g)$ admits a tree-foliation $\{\Sigma_t\}_{t\in T}$ satisfying, for every $t\in T$,

$$
\operatorname{diam}(\Sigma_t)\leq \frac{C}{\sqrt{\Lambda_0}},\qquad \operatorname{Area}(\Sigma_t)\leq \frac{C}{\Lambda_0}.
$$

Such a foliation would provide the small-area and small-intrinsic-diameter sphere foliation needed to construct a continuously varying sweepout by short closed curves. The statement is presented as a conjectural ingredient in the paper; no resolution is supplied here.
quantifiers_and_scope: One universal C for every metric S3 with scalar lower bound Lambda0 and every foliation leaf.
individual_disposition: Tree-foliation regularity, singular leaves and admissible parameter maps are unspecified. Diameter control is intrinsic, so ambient width bounds do not suffice. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Salez–Youssef conjecture on Ollivier curvature and log-Sobolev inequalities
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $(X,p)$ be a reversible Markov chain. Write $d:=\max\{1/p(x,y):p(x,y)>0\}$ for its sparsity constant, and let $\operatorname{Lip}$ denote the Lipschitz constant with respect to the combinatorial distance, also called the hop-count distance. Suppose that the Ollivier curvature is bounded below by $K>0$, in the sense that

$$
\operatorname{Lip}(P_t f)\leq e^{-Kt}\operatorname{Lip}(f)\quad\text{for all }f\in\mathbb{R}^X\text{ and }t>0.
$$

**Salez–Youssef conjecture.** There is a universal constant $c>0$ such that

$$
\alpha_{LSI}\geq c\cdot\frac{K}{\log d}.
$$

Salez and Youssef established the analogous estimate under a Bakry–Émery curvature lower bound, while the Ollivier-curvature version would avoid the stronger non-negative sectional-curvature assumption and is often easier to compute in practice. The conjecture is presented here as the subject of the paper; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
quantifiers_and_scope: One universal c for reversible chains with positive Ollivier contraction K and sparsity d.
individual_disposition: Finite-state/irreducibility assumptions, LSI normalization, and d=1 endpoint require source restoration; Bakry-Emery analogue is not a bridge to the stated curvature. HOLD_SCOPE.

title: Genus-zero mirror-map conjecture for complete intersections in weighted projective space
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $P(a_1,\dots,a_N\mid k_1,\dots,k_m)$ be a nonsingular complete intersection in weighted projective space. Let $t^p(x^*)$ be the mirror maps defined from the genus-zero virtual structure constants, and let $x^p(t^*)$ denote their inverse. Write $\langle{\mathcal O}_{h^a}{\mathcal O}_{h^b}\rangle_0(t^*)$ for the genus-zero two-point Gromov--Witten generating function and $w({\mathcal O}_{h^a}{\mathcal O}_{h^b})_0(x^*)$ for the corresponding virtual structure-constant generating function. **Genus-zero mirror-map conjecture.** For all admissible $a$ and $b$, 

$$
\langle{\mathcal O}_{h^a} {\mathcal O}_{h^b}\rangle_{0}\bigl(t^0,t^1,t^2,\dots,t^{N-m-1}\bigr)=w({\mathcal O}_{h^a} {\mathcal O}_{h^b})_{0}\bigl(x^0(t^*),x^1(t^*),x^2(t^*),\dots,x^{N-m-1}(t^*)\bigr).
$$

 This change-of-variables assertion is used to compute genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants; the source states that it was already proved for projective hypersurfaces, while its status for the stated weighted complete intersections is not specified.
quantifiers_and_scope: All nonsingular weighted complete intersections and all admissible a,b, equality of full generating series.
individual_disposition: Mirror maps, virtual constants and admissibility are source-defined. Projective hypersurface results do not settle weighted complete intersections. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Kwan–Wigderson's unbounded inertia conjecture for graphs with independence number two
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a simple graph, and let $\alpha(G)$ denote its independence number. A weighted adjacency matrix of $G$ is a Hermitian matrix $A$ indexed by $V$ such that $A_{ij}\neq 0$ only when $ij\in E$. For a Hermitian matrix $A$, let $n_{\geq 0}(A)$ be the number of nonnegative eigenvalues, and define $n_{\geq 0}(G)$ as the minimum of $n_{\geq 0}(A)$ over all weighted adjacency matrices $A$ of $G$.

**Kwan–Wigderson's conjecture.** For every integer $k$, there exists a graph $G$ with $\alpha(G)=2$ and

$$
n_{\geq 0}(A)\geq k
$$

for every weighted adjacency matrix $A$ of $G$.

This conjecture concerns whether the inertia bound $\alpha(G)\leq n_{\geq 0}(G)$ can be arbitrarily far from tight, even among graphs with independence number two. It arose from work on Godsil's question about whether the inertia bound can always be attained by a suitable weighted adjacency matrix; the source provides no resolution of the conjecture.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every integer k exists graph alpha=2 such that every supported Hermitian adjacency matrix has at least k nonnegative eigenvalues.
individual_disposition: Quantifier over all complex weights defeats a single spectral calculation; need a graph family with a uniform inertia obstruction. PARK_DEEP.

title: Principal-pair spectral conjecture for orthorecursive coefficients
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $(c_n)_{n\geq 0}$ be the orthorecursive coefficients, and let $g^*$ be the function whose zero with smallest positive real part is

$$
\rho_1=\alpha_1+i\tau_1,
$$

where $\alpha_1\approx1.34652$ and $\tau_1\approx1.05516$. The constants $A$, $\varphi$, and $\kappa$ below are real or complex as specified. **Principal-pair conjecture.** There exist a nonzero constant $\kappa\in\mathbb{C}$ and a real number $\sigma>\alpha_1$ such that

$$
c_n=2\operatorname{Re}\left(\kappa n^{-1-\rho_1}\right)+O\left(n^{-1-\sigma}\right) \qquad (n\to\infty).
$$

Equivalently,

$$
c_n=A n^{-1-\alpha_1}\sin(\tau_1\log n+\varphi)+O(n^{-1-\sigma}),
$$

for suitable real constants $A\ne0$ and $\varphi$. This refines the preceding oscillatory conjecture by predicting $\delta=1+\alpha_1$ and $P=\tau_1$; it remains unproved, while the paper establishes only $c_n=O(n^{-2})$.
quantifiers_and_scope: Exists nonzero kappa and sigma>alpha1 controlling every coefficient as n tends to infinity.
individual_disposition: Neither coefficient recursion nor g* is defined; zero locations alone do not establish a nonzero residue or remainder bound. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: A depth-bounded local converse conjecture for supercuspidal representations of general linear groups
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $F$ be the underlying non-Archimedean local field, let $ n$ be a positive integer, and let $ \pi_{1}$ and $ \pi_{2}$ be irreducible supercuspidal representations of $\operatorname{GL}(n,F)$ with the same central character. For a representation $ \rho$, write $d(\rho)$ for its depth, and let $ \psi_F$ be the fixed nontrivial additive character of $F$. **Depth-bounded local converse conjecture.** If

$$
\gamma(s,\pi_{1}\times\tau,\psi_F)=\gamma(s,\pi_{2}\times\tau,\psi_F)
$$

for every irreducible supercuspidal representation $ \tau$ of $\operatorname{GL}(r,F)$ with $1\leq r\leq\left\lfloor\frac n2\right\rfloor$ and $d(\tau)\leq d(\pi_i)$, then $ \pi_1\cong\pi_2$. This proposes that, once the central character is fixed, twists of bounded depth up to the middle rank should determine a supercuspidal representation.
quantifiers_and_scope: All same-central-character supercuspidal pairs and twists of each rank up to floor(n/2), with bounded depths.
individual_disposition: The subscript i in d(tau)<=d(pi_i) leaves joint versus either depth unclear; finite twist tests are not full local converse. HOLD_SCOPE.

title: Characterization conjecture for well-hued graphs with linear colorability sequence
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected well-hued graph, let $\alpha(G)$ be its independence number, and let $k=\chi(G)$ be its chromatic number. Its colorability sequence is the sequence of maximum orders of induced $i$-colorable subgraphs. For graphs $H_1,\dots,H_k$, write $K_{\alpha(G),\dots,\alpha(G)}$ for the complete $k$-partite graph whose $k$ parts each have size $\alpha(G)$, and let $N_G[u]$ denote the closed neighborhood of $u$. **Characterization conjecture.** $G$ has colorability sequence

$$
(\alpha(G),2\alpha(G),3\alpha(G),\dots,k\alpha(G))
$$

and chromatic number $k$ if and only if $G$ is a spanning subgraph of $K_{\alpha(G),\dots,\alpha(G)}$ such that, for every $u\in V(G)$, the graph induced by $V(G)\setminus N_G[u]$ is $\overline{K_{\alpha(G)}}$-free.
This conjecture seeks an intrinsic characterization of the connected well-hued graphs whose colorability sequence is $(\alpha(G),2\alpha(G),\dots,k\alpha(G))$. The supplied text gives no evidence that it is resolved.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every connected well-hued graph, equivalence for its full colorability sequence and every closed neighborhood.
individual_disposition: Well-hued is undefined; dropping it risks a routine coloring identity for a different class. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Strong Watanabe–Yoshida conjecture for Hilbert–Kunz multiplicity
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $d\geq 2$. Set

$$
R_{p,d}:=\mathbb{F}_p[[x_0,\ldots,x_d]]/(Q_d),
$$

where

$$
Q_d=\begin{cases}x_0x_1+x_2x_3+\dots+x_{d-1}x_d & \text{if $d$ is odd},\\x_0x_1+x_2x_3+\dots+x_{d-2}x_{d-1}+x_d^2 & \text{if $d$ is even}.
\end{cases}
$$

Let $(R,\mathfrak{m},k)$ be an unmixed non-regular local ring of characteristic $p$ and dimension $d$. Here, unmixed means that $\dim \widehat{R}/\mathfrak{p}=\dim \widehat{R}$ for every $\mathfrak{p}\in\operatorname{Ass}(\widehat{R})$. **Strong Watanabe–Yoshida conjecture.** The following assertions hold:

1. $e_{\operatorname{HK}}(R)\geq e_{\operatorname{HK}}(R_{p,d})$.
2. If $e_{\operatorname{HK}}(R)=e_{\operatorname{HK}}(R_{p,d})$, then $\widehat{R}\cong R_{p,d}\widehat{\otimes}_{\mathbb{F}_p}k$; that is, the completion of $R$ is isomorphic to the coordinate ring of a quadric hypersurface.
3. $e_{\operatorname{HK}}(R_{p,d})\geq 1+c_d$, where $c_d$ are the coefficients of the Taylor expansion of $\sec x+\tan x$.

The first two assertions give a lower bound for Hilbert–Kunz multiplicity and characterize the rings attaining the minimum. The third gives a characteristic-free lower bound; it is known for sufficiently large $p$ and, according to the source, for all $p\geq 3$, while the full conjecture remains open.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every dimension d>=2, characteristic p and unmixed nonregular local ring, all three claims including rigidity.
individual_disposition: Residue-field/coefficient-field assumptions needed for completed tensor-product isomorphism; stated large-characteristic partial results are not full scope. HOLD_SCOPE.

title: Rémond's Dobrowolski conjecture for finite-rank subgroups
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $K$ be a number field, let $G$ be a semiabelian variety over $K$, and let $\Gamma\subset G(\overline{K})$ be a subgroup of finite rank. For a subvariety $V\subset G$, write $\mu_{\mathrm{ess}}(V)$ for its essential minimum and $\omega_{K(\Gamma)}(V)$ for its obstruction index relative to $K(\Gamma)$. Call $\Gamma$ a **Dobrowolski group** if, for every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $c_\Gamma(\varepsilon)>0$ such that

$$
\omega_{K(\Gamma)}(V)^{1+\varepsilon}\mu_{\mathrm{ess}}(V)\geq c_\Gamma(\varepsilon)
$$

for every $\Gamma$-transverse subvariety $V\subset G$. **Rémond's Dobrowolski conjecture.** Every subgroup of $G(\overline{K})$ of finite rank is a Dobrowolski group. This is stated as a weaker form of Rémond's Lehmer conjecture and is sufficient for the special case pursued in the paper; the supplied text does not state that it is solved.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every finite-rank subgroup of every semiabelian variety over a number field, each epsilon>0 and every transverse V.
individual_disposition: Gamma-transverse and obstruction-index conventions are missing; no elementary height bound covers this uniformity. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Bogulavsky's conjecture on degrees of common zero sets
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field, let $V(W)$ be the common zero set of a subspace $W$ of $S_d(m,\mathbb{F}_q)$, and let $\omega_r(d,m)=(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{m+1})$ be the $r$th largest element, in lexicographical order, of the degree-$d$ exponent tuples. For a projective variety, write $\deg_i(V(W))$ for its degree in dimension $i$. Suppose $m,d\geq1$ and $1\leq r\leq\binom{m+d}{d}$. **Bogulavsky's conjecture.** For every $r$-dimensional subspace $W$ of $S_d(m,\mathbb{F}_q)$,

$$
\Big(\deg_{m-1}(V(W)),\dots,\deg_0(V(W)),d-\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}\deg_i(V(W))\Big)\leq_{\operatorname{lex}}(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_{m+1}),
$$

and equality holds for some $W$. The conjecture concerns sharp lexicographic bounds on the degrees of common zero sets in different dimensions. The supplied text recalls it as a conjecture and gives no evidence of resolution.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every m,d>=1, all admissible r, every r-plane W, plus an attaining W.
individual_disposition: S_d, scheme versus reduced common zero set, and dimensional-degree conventions are not supplied; known point-count counterexamples cannot automatically refute this lex-degree formulation. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Propagation-time interval conjecture for minimum zero forcing sets of hypercubes
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $Q_d$ be the $d$-dimensional hypercube graph. A **minimum zero forcing set** is a zero forcing set of cardinality equal to the zero forcing number of $Q_d$; its propagation time is the number of parallel forcing rounds needed to color all vertices. Let $\operatorname{pt}(Q_d)$ and $\operatorname{PT}(Q_d)$ denote the minimum and maximum propagation times, respectively, among minimum zero forcing sets of $Q_d$. A graph has a **full propagation time interval** if it has minimum zero forcing sets with every integer propagation time between $\operatorname{pt}(Q_d)$ and $\operatorname{PT}(Q_d)$. 

**Propagation-time interval conjecture.** For every $d\geq 2$, 

$$
\operatorname{pt}(Q_d)=1 \quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{PT}(Q_d)=2^{d-2}.
$$

Moreover, $Q_d$ has a full propagation time interval.

The preceding results establish the existence of minimum zero forcing sets with propagation times $1$, $2$, $3$, and $4$ for $d\geq 4$, and hence already give non-automorphic minimum zero forcing sets. The conjecture predicts the complete range of propagation times through the claimed maximum $2^{d-2}$; the source states that this remains open, together with the enumeration of all minimum zero forcing sets of $Q_d$.
quantifiers_and_scope: All d>=2: minimum time 1, maximum 2^(d-2), and every integer between for minimum forcing sets.
individual_disposition: Constructing times 1 through 4 does not bound the maximum over every minimum set. No full-scope recursive upper bound established. PARK_DEEP.

title: The Large Galois Orbits conjecture for endomorphism-generic PEL subvarieties
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $g\geq 3$, let $C$ be an irreducible algebraic curve in $\mathcal{A}_g$, and let $S$ be the smallest special subvariety of $\mathcal{A}_g$ containing $C$. Let $\Omega$ be the set of special subvarieties of $\mathcal{A}_g$ of simple PEL type III or IV and dimension at most $\dim(S)-2$. Let $\Sigma$ be the set of points in $\mathcal{A}_g(\mathbb{C})$ that are endomorphism generic in some member of $\Omega$. Let $L\subset\mathbb{C}$ be a finitely generated subfield over which $C$ is defined, and write $A_s$ for the abelian variety associated with $s$.

**Large Galois Orbits conjecture.** There exist positive constants $C_{\mathrm{mult}}$ and $C_{\mathrm{exp}}$ such that, for all $s\in C\cap\Sigma$,

$$
\#\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{C}/L)\cdot s\geq C_{\mathrm{mult}}\,\bigl|\operatorname{disc}(\operatorname{End}(A_s))\bigr|^{C_{\mathrm{exp}}}.
$$

This is presented as the natural generalisation of the earlier large Galois-orbit conjecture. It is used to obtain finiteness for the intersection $C\cap\Sigma$, but no resolution is supplied in the text.
quantifiers_and_scope: For each curve and field of definition exist positive constants, uniformly for all points in C intersect Sigma.
individual_disposition: Endomorphism genericity and simple PEL types require precise definitions; discriminant orbit estimate is a deep arithmetic input. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Local-resilience conjecture for structurally stable color-biased Hamilton cycles
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with an edge-coloring using $r$ colors, and let $m$ be the color-bias threshold. A graph is said to satisfy the relevant local resilience condition if, for every subset $U\subseteq V(G)$ with $|U|\le Cm$, the induced subgraph $G\setminus U$ contains a Hamilton cycle.

**Local-resilience conjecture.** There exists a sufficiently large constant $C>0$ such that, whenever $G$ satisfies this local resilience condition and every Hamilton cycle in $G$ has color-bias less than $m$, $G$ must structurally resemble one of the known extremal constructions.

This conjecture proposes replacing a minimum-degree hypothesis with a robust local resilience condition in the structural theory of color-balanced Hamilton cycles. The surrounding discussion indicates that the necessity of the additive degree term is unclear for $r\geq 3$, while stronger stability statements remain a natural direction for future research.
quantifiers_and_scope: Exists sufficiently large C, all r-colored graphs resilient under deletions of at most Cm vertices.
individual_disposition: Structurally resemble known extremal constructions gives no metric, family or error quantifiers; cannot be treated as a complete proposition. HOLD_INCOMPLETE.

title: Schneider's support conjecture for mixed Hessian measures
exact_utf8_statement:
Fix an open convex set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $\operatorname{Conv}(\Omega)$ be the set of proper convex functions $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\Omega\subseteq\mathop{\mathrm{dom}} f$. For $f\in\operatorname{Conv}(\Omega)$ and $x\in\Omega$, let $L(f,x)$ be the largest convex subset of $\Omega$ on which $f$ is affine and that has $x$ in its relative interior, and set $\bar L(f,x)=\operatorname{span}\{L(f,x)-x\}$. A point $x\in\Omega$ is **$(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$-extreme** if

$$
\dim\big(\bar L(f_I,x)^\perp\big)\geq |I|
$$

for every $I\subseteq[n]$.

**Schneider's conjecture.** For $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in\operatorname{Conv}(\Omega)$, the mixed Hessian measure satisfies

$$
\mathop{\mathrm{supp}} \mathrm{H}_{f_1,\ldots,f_n}=\mathop{\mathrm{cl}}\big\{x\in\Omega:x\text{ is }(f_1,\ldots,f_n)\text{-extreme}\big\}.
$$

This is the convex-function analogue of Schneider's conjectural support characterization for mixed area measures. The source presents it as a transcription of that conjecture, and no resolution is supplied.
quantifiers_and_scope: All n-tuples of proper convex functions and every subset I in the extremality condition.
individual_disposition: The function f_I and mixed Hessian normalization/domain of closure are unspecified; no support theorem inferred from analogy to area measures. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Conjecture on the smallest bulk gap for real Wigner matrices
exact_utf8_statement:
Fix $
\alpha>0$. Let $
\mu_1\leq\cdots\leq\mu_N$ be the eigenvalues of a GOE matrix, and let $
\lambda_1\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_N$ be the eigenvalues of a real generalized Wigner matrix $(H_N)$ with uniform $p$-support, where $p\geq2$. **Smallest-gap convergence conjecture.** For some sufficiently large $p$, for all sufficiently large $N$,

$$
d_{\mathrm K}\biggl(\min_{\alpha N\leq k\leq(1-\alpha)N}N^{3/2}(\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k),\min_{\alpha N\leq k\leq(1-\alpha)N}N^{3/2}(\mu_{k+1}-\mu_k)\biggr)=o(1).
$$

A stronger conjecture states that $p=2$ is enough. In particular, together with the cited GOE smallest-gap law, the conjecture predicts a constant $C=C(\alpha)$ such that, for every $x\geq0$, the distribution function converges to $\int_0^x2u e^{-u^2}\,du$. The source gives no resolution status.
quantifiers_and_scope: Some sufficiently large moment parameter p, every real generalized Wigner ensemble, fixed bulk alpha, N tending to infinity.
individual_disposition: Uniform p-support is undefined and alpha>0 alone allows empty bulk interval for alpha>=1/2. Need exact source assumptions before comparison. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Optimized full inexact gradient descent has a superlinear numerical rate for residual gradient minimization
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $N$ denote the iteration count and let the performance criterion be the minimum squared gradient norm, $\min_{k\in\{1,\ldots,N\}}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|^2$, for minimizing a smooth convex function with relative inexactness level $\epsilon$. Consider full inexact gradient descent, whose updates may use all past inexact gradient information, with numerically optimized step sizes. **Optimized full inexact gradient descent conjecture.** Full inexact gradient descent with optimized step sizes can achieve a faster convergence rate than

$$
\mathcal{O}(1/N)
$$

for minimizing the squared gradient norm. The reported rates for $\epsilon=0.1,0.3,0.5$ are respectively $\mathcal{O}(1/N^{1.384})$, $\mathcal{O}(1/N^{1.342})$, and $\mathcal{O}(1/N^{1.190})$. These are numerical fits, and the source does not provide a theoretical proof of the rates.
quantifiers_and_scope: Existence of optimized full inexact gradient scheme with o(1/N)-type squared-gradient performance for an inexactness regime.
individual_disposition: No exact error oracle, constants, initialization radius or rate quantifiers; fitted exponents are not theoretical convergence statements. HOLD_INCOMPLETE.

title: The non-CM Fourier coefficient conjecture for odd discriminant level
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $k$ be an integer with $k\geq 3$, and let $D=p_1\cdots p_\ell$ be an odd discriminant. Let $S_k^{\mathrm{Ell}}(\Gamma_1(D),\omega_{E/\mathbb{Q}})$ denote the space of elliptic cusp forms of weight $k$, level $\Gamma_1(D)$, and nebentypus $\omega_{E/\mathbb{Q}}$. A normalized newform in this space is **non-CM** if it does not have complex multiplication. **The non-CM Fourier coefficient conjecture.** If this space contains a non-CM normalized newform, then at least one such newform $f$ satisfies

$$
a_f(p_i)\neq \pm p_i^{(k-1)/2}\quad\text{for every }i.
$$

Here $a_f(p_i)$ is the $p_i$-th Fourier coefficient of $f$. This conjecture asserts that, among the available non-CM newforms, one can find a form avoiding the CM-type extremal values at every prime dividing the odd discriminant. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every k>=3 and odd discriminant D, existence of one non-CM form avoiding both extremal coefficients at every prime divisor.
individual_disposition: Field E and character interpretation are not specified; coefficient bounds on unramified primes do not decide ramified-prime simultaneous avoidance. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Pokrovskiy's semidegree conjecture for linked tournaments
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$. A **tournament** is a digraph obtained by orienting each edge of a complete graph in exactly one direction. For a tournament $D$, let $\delta^+(D)$ and $\delta^-(D)$ denote its minimum out-degree and minimum in-degree, respectively, and let

$$
\delta^0(D)=\min\{\delta^+(D),\delta^-(D)\}
$$

denote its minimum semidegree. A tournament is $k$-linked if every $2k$ distinct vertices can be paired in the prescribed order by $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths.

**Pokrovskiy's conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists an integer $h(k)$ such that every $2k$-connected tournament with $\delta^0(D)\geq h(k)$ is $k$-linked.

The conjecture was disproved by a family of $2k$-connected tournaments with sufficiently large order and minimum semidegree that are not $k$-linked. Thus connectivity at least $2k+1$ is necessary when the minimum semidegree is prescribed as a function of $k$.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every k exists h(k), all 2k-connected tournaments above semidegree h(k).
individual_disposition: Literal record explicitly reports a disproving family. Treat as a reported public resolution pending actual body, not a fresh counterexample; no proof-body clearance claimed. HOLD_REPORTED_RESOLUTION.

title: Zhang et al.'s AVD total coloring conjecture
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite, simple, undirected graph. For each vertex $u$, let $N_G(u)$ be its set of neighbours, let $\partial_G(u)$ be the set of edges incident with $u$, and let $\partial_G^\star(u)=\{u\}\cup\partial_G(u)$. Write $\Delta(G)$ for the maximum degree of $G$. An **adjacent vertex distinguishing (AVD) total coloring** is a proper total coloring $\phi:V(G)\cup E(G)\to C$ such that $\phi(\partial_G^\star(u))\ne\phi(\partial_G^\star(v))$ for every edge $uv\in E(G)$. **AVD Total Coloring Conjecture.** Every graph $G$ has an AVD total coloring using at most $\Delta(G)+3$ colors.

The conjecture is a strengthening of the total coloring problem, requiring adjacent vertices to have distinct sets of colors on their incident vertices and edges. The source attributes it to Zhang et al.; the supplied text does not establish whether it is resolved in full.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every finite simple graph admits proper AVD total coloring with at most Delta+3 colors.
individual_disposition: Would entail a full total-coloring-strength construction, including all maximum degrees; special families or greedy larger palettes cannot settle it. PARK_DEEP.

title: Randomly shifted Gumbel limit for the maximum of the two-dimensional inhomogeneous DGFF
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $d=2$ and suppose that Assumption~-(i) and the moment condition~ hold, in particular $\operatorname{\mathbb{P}}[\omega(e)>0]=1$ for $e\in E_d$. For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, set

$$
M_n:=\max_{x\in[-n,n]\cap\mathbb{Z}^d}\varphi_x^{\Lambda_n},\qquad \Lambda_n:=[-n,n]^d,
$$

and

$$
m_n:=\sqrt{\bar g}\left(\sqrt{2d}\log n-\frac{3}{2\sqrt{2d}}\log\log n\right),
$$

where $\bar g$ is as in. **Randomly shifted Gumbel limit conjecture.** For $\operatorname{\mathbb{P}}$-almost every $\omega$, under $\operatorname{\mathbf{P}}^\omega$, $M_n-m_n$ converges in law to a randomly shifted Gumbel distribution: there exist $\beta^*\in(0,\infty)$ and a random variable $Z$ such that, for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{\mathbf{P}}^\omega[M_n-m_n\leq t]=\operatorname{\mathbf{E}}^\omega\left[\exp\left(-\beta^*Z\exp(-\sqrt{2d}t)\right)\right].
$$

The result would identify the extremal fluctuations of the two-dimensional inhomogeneous DGFF, whose correlations and random conductances make the maximum substantially more intricate than in the homogeneous model. The source presents this as an open problem; it also conjectures that $Z$ is the limit of variables resembling the derivative martingale from critical Gaussian multiplicative chaos and branching processes.
quantifiers_and_scope: Almost every conductance environment in dimension two, all real t, quenched centered-maximum convergence.
individual_disposition: Assumption-(i), moment condition and definition of bar g are absent and text is visibly truncated. HOLD_INCOMPLETE.

title: The partite folklore clique decomposition conjecture
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $(V_1,\ldots,V_q)$ be a balanced $q$-partition of a $q$-partite graph $G$, with $|V_i|=n$ for every $i$. Define

$$
\hat{\delta}(G):=\min\{d(v,V_j):1\leq j\leq q,\ v\in V(G)\setminus V_j\}.
$$

Call $G$ **partite-$K_q$-divisible** when, for every $1\leq j_1<j_2\leq q$ and every $v\in V(G)\setminus(V_{j_1}\cup V_{j_2})$, one has $d(v,V_{j_1})=d(v,V_{j_2})$.

**Partite folklore conjecture.** For each integer $q\geq 4$, the following holds for sufficiently large $n$: if $G$ is a balanced partite-$K_q$-divisible $q$-partite graph on $qn$ vertices with

$$
\hat{\delta}(G)\geq \left(1-\frac{1}{q+1}\right)n,
$$

then $G$ admits a $K_q$-decomposition.

This is the partite counterpart of the folklore high-minimum-degree conjecture for $K_q$-decompositions and is connected to the existence of mutually orthogonal Latin squares. The source presents it as open.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every q>=4 and all sufficiently large n, balanced divisible q-partite graphs at the stated partite degree threshold.
individual_disposition: Sharp threshold requires an all-input absorption/decomposition argument; complete multipartite and Latin-square instances are insufficient. PARK_DEEP.

title: Interaction-strength conjecture for Bouw-Möller surfaces with divisible parameters
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $S_{m,n}$ be the Bouw-Möller surface associated with integers $m,n\geq 2$, and let $\operatorname{Int}(\alpha,\beta)$ denote the intersection number of closed curves $\alpha,\beta$, with $l(\alpha)$ and $l(\beta)$ their lengths. Suppose that $m,n\geq 3$, $(m,n)\neq(3,3)$, and $m$ is a multiple of $n$. Set

$$
l_0=\sin\frac{\pi}{m}.
$$

**Interaction-strength conjecture.** For every pair of closed curves $\alpha,\beta$ on $S_{m,n}$,

$$
\frac{\operatorname{Int}(\alpha,\beta)}{l(\alpha)l(\beta)}\leq\frac{1}{4l_0^2}.
$$

Moreover, equality is achieved by two closed curves $\alpha,\beta$ each made of two sides of length $l_0$ and intersecting once. The conjecture concerns the case excluded from the preceding theorem, where the equality construction with curves intersecting twice does not apply; it would determine the algebraic interaction strength for these Bouw-Möller surfaces when $m$ is a multiple of $n$.
quantifiers_and_scope: All m,n>=3 with n dividing m except (3,3), every pair of closed curves, plus equality construction.
individual_disposition: Surface metric/gluing and algebraic versus geometric intersection need definitions; dividing-parameter restriction is essential. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: The linear-or-bounded conjecture for induced poset saturation
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite poset. For a family $\mathcal F$ of subsets of $[n]$, call $\mathcal F$ **$\mathcal P$-saturated** if it contains no induced copy of $\mathcal P$, but $\mathcal F\cup\{S\}$ contains an induced copy of $\mathcal P$ for every $S\notin\mathcal F$. Write $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,\mathcal P)$ for the smallest size of a $\mathcal P$-saturated family.

**The linear-or-bounded conjecture.** For every finite poset $\mathcal P$, the induced saturated number $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,\mathcal P)$ is either bounded, or at least linear in $n$.

Earlier results showed that the induced saturated number for every poset is either bounded or at least logarithmic in $n$, and later at least $2\sqrt n$. The conjecture asserts that the lower-growth alternative can always be strengthened to linear growth.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every finite poset P: its induced saturation function is uniformly bounded or Omega(n).
individual_disposition: Need an arbitrary-poset growth dichotomy, not constructions for a fixed poset. No full lower-bound mechanism beyond existing sublinear bounds established. PARK_DEEP.

title: Győri–Keszegh's greedy-partition triangle conjecture for $K_4$-free graphs
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex $K_4$-free graph with $e$ edges. A **greedy partition** $P$ of $G$ is a partition of $V(G)$ into disjoint cliques $T_i$ such that $|T_i|\geq |T_{i+1}|$ for each $i$, and for every $\ell\geq 1$, the union of cliques of size at most $\ell$ induces a $K_{\ell+1}$-free subgraph. Write $r:=r(P)$ for the number of cliques in $P$, let $t(G)$ be the number of triangles in $G$, and let $t_e(G)$ be the maximum number of edge-disjoint triangles in $G$. Define

$$
g(G,P):=r(e-r(n-r))-t(G).
$$

**Győri–Keszegh's conjecture.** For every such graph $G$ and every greedy partition $P$,

$$
t(G)\geq r\bigl(e-r(n-r)\bigr),\qquad\text{equivalently }g(G,P)\leq 0,
$$

and consequently

$$
t_e(G)\geq e-r(n-r).
$$

The conjecture strengthens the known triangle bound used by Győri and Keszegh to derive the extremal result that every $K_4$-free graph with $t_{n,2}+m$ edges contains at least $m$ edge-disjoint triangles. A greedy-partition lemma gives $t_e(G)\geq t(G)/r(P)$, so the conjectured inequality would imply the stated lower bound for edge-disjoint triangles; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every K4-free graph and every greedy clique partition, both triangle inequality and consequent packing inequality.
individual_disposition: Exact cubic statistic depends on all greedy partitions; no universal symmetrization monotonicity or finite counterexample established. PARK_DEEP.

title: Five-color version of the planar equitable coloring theorem
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph, and let $w_0,w_1$ be its two vertices with largest degrees, breaking ties arbitrarily. Let $s\ge 40$. If there exist disjoint independent sets $I_0,I_1$ such that

$$
|I_0|=\left\lfloor\frac{n}{s}\right\rfloor,
\qquad |I_1|=\left\lfloor\frac{n+1}{s}\right\rfloor,
$$

and $w_0,w_1\in I_0\cup I_1$, then $G$ has an equitable $s$-coloring.

**Five-color planar theorem conjecture.** The same statement remains true when the lower bound $s\ge 40$ is replaced by $s\ge 5$.

The paper proves the planar theorem for $s\ge 40$ and conjectures that the threshold can be reduced to $5$. The conjecture concerns strengthening the sufficient condition for equitable colorability of planar graphs; the authors note that they have not optimized the proved bound and believe it is far from best possible.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every planar graph and every integer s>=5 satisfying the two disjoint-independent-set conditions on highest-degree vertices.
individual_disposition: The conditional theorem is stronger than ordinary equitable coloring of bounded-degree families; threshold reduction needs a uniform recoloring mechanism. PARK_DEEP.

title: The generalized ballot property for labeled chips on k-ary trees
exact_utf8_statement: Let $N_{k,\ell}$ denote the number of labeled chips starting at the root of a $k$-ary tree in the setting of the paper, and let a stable configuration be one obtained from these chips by chip-firing. For a vertex $v$, let its children be ordered from left to right. **Generalized ballot property.** For every stable configuration resulting from $N_{k,\ell}$ labeled chips starting at the root, every vertex $v$, every $i\in\{1,2,\dots,N_{k,\ell-1}\}$, and every $a,b\in\{1,2,\dots,k\}$ with $a<b$, the $i$th smallest chip in the subtree rooted at the $a$th leftmost child of $v$ is less than the $i$th smallest chip in the subtree rooted at the $b$th leftmost child of $v$. This generalizes the binary ballot property from comparisons between two sides of a vertex to comparisons among all ordered child subtrees; its validity is presented as an open question.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every stable reachable configuration, every vertex, ordered children and each rank through N(k,l-1).
individual_disposition: Firing rule, N(k,l), and ranks for small/empty descendant subtrees are not specified; ordinary chip-firing cannot replace labeled ordered firing. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Gumbel separation-profile conjecture for the random transposition shuffle
exact_utf8_statement:
Consider, for $n\geq 2$, the random transposition shuffle $(X_t^{(n)})_{t\geq 0}$ on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$, in discrete or continuous time, and let $\mathrm{d}_{\textup{sep}}^{(n)}(t)$ denote its separation distance to stationarity at time $t\geq 0$. For any $c\in\mathbb{R}$, **the Gumbel separation-profile conjecture** asserts that

$$
\mathrm{d}_{\textup{sep}}^{(n)}\left(\left\lfloor \frac{1}{2}n(\ln n+c)\right\rfloor\right)\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}1-e^{-e^{-c}}.
$$

In words, the separation profile for random transpositions should be given by a Gumbel distribution. The conjecture is motivated by the likelihood calculation for $n$-cycles and would follow from a positive answer to the question of whether, for every time, the minimum of likelihood is attained at $n$-cycles. Its resolution is not supplied here.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every fixed real c, asymptotic separation for discrete or continuous random transpositions.
individual_disposition: Discrete-time laziness convention is essential because nonlazy transpositions have parity obstruction; endpoint convention corrections earn no credit. HOLD_SCOPE.

title: The monotonicity conjecture for diagonal $(m,m)$-town families modulo $k$
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, let $\mathscr{P}(n)$ be the power set of $[n]$, and let a family be an $(a,b)$-town modulo $k$ when all its sets have cardinality congruent to $a$ modulo $k$ and every pair of distinct sets has intersection cardinality congruent to $b$ modulo $k$. For $i=1,2$, let $\mathcal{F}_i\subseteq\mathscr{P}(n)$ be a $(m_i,m_i)$-town modulo $k$ family of maximum size, where $0\leq m_1,m_2\leq k-1$. **Monotonicity conjecture.** If $m_1<m_2$, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}_1|\geq |\mathcal{F}_2|.
$$

This conjecture arises from numerical evidence and concerns the relative sizes of diagonal town families when the modulus $k$ need not be prime. The linear upper bound $n$ is already known when the two town parameters differ modulo some prime divisor of $k$; the remaining cases, particularly those with $a\equiv b$ modulo every prime divisor of $k$, are not fully understood.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every positive n, modulus k>=2 and 0<=m1<m2<k: exact diagonal-town maxima are nonincreasing.
individual_disposition: Primary definition and final conjecture read. Exact maximum-clique checks for n=1..8,k=2..8 find no violation; no injection/upper-bound mechanism for all composite moduli. PARK_NO_FULL_SCOPE_ROUTE.

title: Gullerud–Johnson–Mbirika conjectures on roots of Fibonacci-shifted path polynomials
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $P_n$ be the path graph on $n$ vertices, let

$$
f_n(\lambda)=\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}(-1)^{n+k}\binom{n-k}{k}\lambda^{n-2k}
$$

be its characteristic polynomial, and let $F_0=0$, $F_1=1$, with $F_n$ denoting the Fibonacci numbers. For each $n$, let $R_n$ be the set of roots of $f_n(\lambda)=F_{n+1}$. **Gullerud–Johnson–Mbirika conjectures.** The following assertions hold: (1) for each $n$, the points in $R_n$ lie on an ellipse; (2) the maximum real part of a point in $R_n$ is unbounded as $n$ increases; (3) for all $n$, the imaginary parts of points in $R_n$ lie within $[-1,1]$; (4) if $n$ is even, then $R_n$ contains exactly two distinct real roots; and (5) if $n$ is odd, then $R_n$ contains exactly one real root, which is negative. These conjectures concern the geometric distribution of roots of characteristic polynomials associated with path graphs. The source reports partial progress toward two conjectures, an infinite class of polynomials contradicting a third, and evidence against a fourth; the supplied text does not identify which numbered assertions have each status.
quantifiers_and_scope: All n, five claims jointly about every root of f_n(lambda)=F_(n+1).
individual_disposition: Primary Conjecture1.1 and Theorem3.5 proof read. Existing ellipse bound for n divisible by4 uses cited Oyengo Proposition3.3; cannot count that subclass or infer all-n boundedness from it. General target and prior dependency remain HOLD.

title: Glock–Kühn–Osthus high-degree conjecture for hypergraph decompositions
exact_utf8_statement:
For integers $q>r\ge 3$, let $G$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. It is **$K_q^r$-divisible** when, for every $i\in\{0,1,\ldots,r-1\}$ and every $i$-set $S\subseteq V(G)$, the number of edges $e\in G$ containing $S$ is divisible by $\binom{q-i}{r-i}$. Let $\delta_{r-1}(G)$ denote the minimum, over all $(r-1)$-sets $S\subseteq V(G)$, of the number of edges containing $S$.

**Glock–Kühn–Osthus conjecture.** For each integer $r\ge 3$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that, for all integers $q>r$ and all sufficiently large $n$, every $K_q^r$-divisible $r$-graph $G$ on $n$ vertices satisfying

$$
\delta_{r-1}(G)\ge \left(1-\frac{C}{q^{r-1}}\right)n
$$

admits a $K_q^r$-decomposition.

This is a high minimum-degree generalization of the Existence Conjecture for combinatorial designs, extending decomposition questions from graphs to higher-uniformity hypergraphs.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every r>=3 exists C(r)>0, every q>r and all sufficiently large n, every divisible hypergraph of that codegree.
individual_disposition: Would require sharp q dependence in full design decomposition; no bounded certificate can establish all parameters. PARK_DEEP.

title: Root-count conjecture for mutations in admissible Dynkin biagrams
exact_utf8_statement: Let $(\Gamma, \Delta)$ be an admissible Dynkin biagram with $r$ vertices. Let $h_{\Gamma}$ and $h_{\Delta}$ denote the Coxeter numbers associated to the respective components, and consider one period of the tropical $T$-system. A mutation is a $\Gamma$-mutation or a $\Delta$-mutation according to whether the corresponding maximum is attained by the $\Gamma$- or $\Delta$-sum. **Root-count conjecture.** The number of $\Gamma$-mutations in one period is the number of roots in the root systems associated to each $\Gamma$-component, totaling $h_{\Gamma}\cdot r$. Similarly, the number of $\Delta$-mutations in one period is the number of roots in the root systems associated to each $\Delta$-component, totaling $h_{\Delta}\cdot r$. The conjecture has been verified by Sage for all non-ADE families in the paper's classification for small $n$, as well as for all infinite ADE families for small $n$; these computations do not constitute a general proof.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every admissible Dynkin biagram, count both types of mutation over one period.
individual_disposition: Admissibility, period length, initial tropical data and ties in the maximum are undefined; hr root count also needs component normalization. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Conjectured distance threshold for $(4,s)$-Salem sets
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field, let $d\geq 2$, and let $E\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^d$ be a $(4,s)$-Salem set. Let $\alpha(d,4,s)$ be the smallest exponent such that every $(4,s)$-Salem set $E$ with $|E|\gg q^{\alpha(d,4,s)}$ satisfies $|\Delta(E)|\gg q$. **Distance-threshold conjecture for $(4,s)$-Salem sets.** One has

$$
\alpha(d,4,s)=
\begin{cases}
1,& d=2,\ s\in[\tfrac14,\tfrac12],\\[3pt]
\frac{d}{2},& d\ge4\ \text{even},\ s\in[\tfrac14,\tfrac{d+2}{4d}],\\[3pt]
\frac{d+2}{8s},& d\ge4\ \text{even},\ s\in[\tfrac{d+2}{4d},\tfrac12],\\[3pt]
\frac{d+1}{8s},& d\ge3\ \text{odd},\ s\in[\tfrac14,\tfrac12].
\end{cases}
$$

The proposed values are supported by constructions of $(4,s)$-Salem sets with few distances and by known distance results, including the Erdős–Falconer threshold in dimension two and sharp results for sets on spheres or arbitrary sets in other dimensions. The stated thresholds remain conjectural in the general $(4,s)$-Salem setting.
quantifiers_and_scope: All dimensions and listed s ranges, exact optimal exponent for all (4,s)-Salem sets over finite fields.
individual_disposition: Salem Fourier normalization and characteristic restrictions on distance form are missing. Sharp examples alone do not prove matching upper thresholds. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Kalai–Meagher conjecture on intersecting families of triangulations
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $d4f4_n$ denote the set of triangulations of a convex $n$-gon, and let $d4f4_{n-1}$ denote the corresponding set for a convex $(n-1)$-gon. The **independence number** $d6fc(\operatorname{KG}(d4f4_n))$ is the size of the largest family of triangulations in $d4f4_n$ such that any two triangulations intersect.

**Kalai–Meagher conjecture.** For every $n\geq 3$,

$$
\alpha(\operatorname{KG}(\mathcal{T}_n))=|\mathcal{T}_{n-1}|=C_{n-3},
$$

where

$$
C_k=\frac{1}{k+1}\binom{2k}{k}
$$

denotes the $k$th Catalan number.

The conjecture asserts that the largest intersecting family consists of all triangulations containing a fixed diagonal, such as ${1,3}$; these are in bijection with triangulations of a convex $(n-1)$-gon. The statement is presented as an open problem in the paper, and no resolution is supplied.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every n>=3, largest pairwise-intersecting triangulation family has Catalan size C_(n-3).
individual_disposition: Intersecting must mean shared diagonals rather than boundary edges; degenerate n=3 and T_2 need conventions. Small polygon corrections are no discovery. HOLD_SCOPE.

title: Pure transport limit for ascent and descent stability
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a domain, let $\boldsymbol{\beta}\in [L^\infty(\Omega)]^d$ be divergence-free, and let $L$ be the transport operator with inflow boundary conditions,

$$
L u=\boldsymbol{\beta}\cdot\nabla u.
$$

For a discrete scheme, let $T_h$ be the resulting operators, let $G(A)$ denote the graph of an operator $A$, let $\gamma_h$ be the reduced minimum modulus associated with $T_h-\lambda$, and let $\operatorname{asc}$ and $\operatorname{dsc}$ denote ascent and descent. **Pure transport limit.** If

$$
G(T_h-\lambda)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{gap}}G(L-\lambda)
$$

as $h\to0$ and

$$
\liminf_{h\to0}\gamma_h>0,
$$

then, for all sufficiently small $h$,

$$
\operatorname{asc}(T_h-\lambda)=\operatorname{asc}(L-\lambda),\qquad \operatorname{dsc}(T_h-\lambda)=\operatorname{dsc}(L-\lambda).
$$

The claim concerns preservation of ascent and descent under graph-gap convergence when the reduced minimum modulus stays uniformly positive; the supplied text does not establish whether this statement is proved, conjectural, or open.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every admissible transport discretization at lambda, eventually exact ascent and descent under graph-gap and uniform reduced modulus.
individual_disposition: Operator domains, ambient comparison spaces and meaning of T_h are not supplied; classical perturbation adaptation must be checked before investment. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: The Overfull Conjecture for graphs of maximum degree greater than one third their order
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph. Write $\Delta(G)$ for its maximum degree, and call $G$ **overfull** if

$$
|E(G)|>\Delta(G)\left\lfloor\frac{|V(G)|}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

A graph is of **Class 2** when its chromatic index satisfies $\chi'(G)=\Delta(G)+1$.

**Overfull Conjecture.** Let $G$ be a graph of Class $2$ with

$$
\Delta(G)>\frac{|V(G)|}{3}.
$$

Then $G$ contains an overfull subgraph $H$ with $\Delta(H)=\Delta(G)$.

This conjecture of Chetwynd and Hilton would make determining the chromatic index polynomial-time solvable for graphs with maximum degree greater than one third their order. It is known in several dense cases, including when $\Delta(G)\geq |V(G)|-3$ and for sufficiently large graphs with $\Delta(G)\geq(1-\varepsilon)|V(G)|$ for $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/14$, but remains open in general.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every simple Class2 graph with Delta>|V|/3 contains an overfull subgraph of the same maximum degree.
individual_disposition: Matching lower-bound witness does not yield the converse for all dense graphs. No uniform edge-coloring proof or exact obstruction obtained. PARK_DEEP.

title: The bounded-size optimal local realizer conjecture
exact_utf8_statement: Let $P$ be a finite poset. A **local realizer** of $P$ is a family of partial linear extensions whose frequency is the maximum number of partial linear extensions in which any element of $P$ appears, and whose size is the number of partial linear extensions in the family. Write $\operatorname{ldim}(P)$ for the minimum possible frequency of a local realizer of $P$, and $\dim(P)$ for the Dushnik–Miller dimension of $P$. The conjecture asserts the following. **Bounded-size optimal local realizer conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ such that for every poset $P$, there is a local realizer $\mathcal{L}$ of $P$ with frequency exactly $\operatorname{ldim}(P)$ and size at most $f(\dim(P))$. This asks whether an optimal local realizer can always be chosen with size controlled solely by the ordinary dimension of the poset, despite the fact that local realizers can generally be much larger than their frequency. The source describes this as a very bold conjecture and gives no resolution.
quantifiers_and_scope: Exists one function f of ordinary dimension, every finite poset has an optimal-frequency local realizer of at most f(dim P) extensions.
individual_disposition: The literal definition omits which comparable and incomparable pairs a local realizer must witness; ordinary realizers only give frequency dim P, not optimal ldim P. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.

title: Subpolynomial treewidth conjecture for induced-minor-free graphs
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $W_{t\times t}$ be the $t$-by-$t$ hexagonal grid and let $K_{t,t}$ be the complete bipartite graph with both sides of the bipartition of size $t$. For a positive integer $t$, let $\mathcal{C}_t$ be the class of graphs with no induced minor isomorphic to $K_{t,t}$ or $W_{t\times t}$, and let $\mathcal{C}_t^*$ be the subclass consisting of graphs with no clique of size $t$. Here $tw(G)$ denotes the treewidth of a graph $G$. **Subpolynomial treewidth conjecture.** For every $t\in{\mathbb N}$, there is an integer $d=d(t)$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal{C}_t^*$ satisfies

$$
tw(G)\leq\log^d n.
$$

The conjecture predicts a polylogarithmic treewidth bound for graphs excluding fixed induced minors and a fixed-size clique, which would support efficient or quasi-polynomial algorithms for problems such as Maximum Weight Independent Set on these classes. Its resolution is not supplied in the source context.
quantifiers_and_scope: For every t exists d(t) bounding treewidth of all n-vertex graphs with both induced-minor and clique exclusions.
individual_disposition: Small n/logarithm conventions need attention, but endpoint repair is no discovery; arbitrary n structural route absent. HOLD_SCOPE.

title: Extremal formula for Berge linear forests
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}=P_{\ell_1}\cup\dots\cup P_{\ell_k}$ be a linear forest with $k\geq 2$ and $\ell_k\geq\dots\geq\ell_1\geq 3$. Write

$$
\ell_i'=\left\lfloor\frac{\ell_i+1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

For an $r$-uniform hypergraph, let $\mathrm{ex}_r(n,\text{Berge-}\mathcal{P})$ denote the maximum number of hyperedges in an $n$-vertex hypergraph containing no Berge copy of $\mathcal{P}$. **Extremal formula for Berge linear forests.** When $2\leq r\leq\sum_{i=1}^k\ell_i'$, 

$$
\mathrm{ex}_r(n,\text{Berge-}\mathcal{P})=\max\{\mathrm{ex}_r(n,\text{Berge-}P_{\ell_k}),f(n,\ell_i,r)\},
$$

where

$$
f(n,\ell_i,r)=\binom{\sum_{i=1}^k\ell_i'-1}{r-1}\left(n-\sum_{i=1}^k\ell_i'+1\right)+\binom{\sum_{i=1}^k\ell_i'-1}{r}+\mathbb{I}_{\Pi\ell_i}\cdot\binom{\sum_{i=1}^k\ell_i-1}{r-2},
$$

and $\mathbb{I}_{\Pi\ell_i}=0$ if $\prod_{i=1}^k\ell_i$ is odd, while $\mathbb{I}_{\Pi\ell_i}=1$ if $\prod_{i=1}^k\ell_i$ is even. The conjecture extends the single-path extremal formula to arbitrary linear forests; the source says that a similar construction gives the lower bound, but does not provide a proof of the asserted equality.
quantifiers_and_scope: All ordered path lengths >=3, k>=2 and r between2 and sum floor((li+1)/2), purported exact extremal formula.
individual_disposition: No sufficiently-large-n qualification or path edge/vertex convention is stated; these are essential before exploiting an apparent small-n failure. HOLD_SCOPE.

title: Characterization of the stability number of connected graphs
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Write $\gamma_{st}(G)$ for its strong domination number, $\operatorname{st}_{\gamma_{st}}(G)$ for the stability value of $\gamma_{st}$, and $\kappa(G)$ for its vertex connectivity. A vertex set is called **critical for maintaining $\gamma_{st}$** when its removal changes the strong domination number as specified by the stability value.

**Stability characterization conjecture.** For every integer $p\ge 1$,

$$
\operatorname{st}_{\gamma_{st}}(G)=p+1
$$

if and only if all of the following hold:

1. $\kappa(G)\ge p$;
2. $G$ has at least $p+1$ vertices whose removal does not change $\gamma_{st}$;
3. every set of $p$ vertices is contained in some minimum strong dominating set of $G-S$ for some set $S$ with $|S|\le p$; and
4. there exists a set of $p+1$ vertices that is critical for maintaining $\gamma_{st}$.

The conjecture proposes a structural characterization of graphs with prescribed stability value. The source states that the problem of characterizing graphs with a given stability value remains open.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every connected graph and p>=1, equivalence between stability p+1 and four conditions.
individual_disposition: Primary Conjecture3.13 matches but critical-for-maintaining is undefined. Nearby Theorem3.10 uses likely changing as its argument; cannot rely on that as a proved necessity. HOLD_SOURCE_DEPENDENCIES.

title: Generation conjecture for Gorenstein kernels of tautological rings
exact_utf8_statement:
For $g,n\geq 0$, let $d53c^{\mathrm{ct}}_{g,n}$ be the moduli space of stable $n$-pointed curves of compact type, let $d52d^*(d53c^{\mathrm{ct}}_{g,n})$ be its tautological ring, and let $d4aa_{g,n}$ be the Gorenstein kernel. For every $s\times n$ matrix $d538$, let $d6a5_{g,\mathsf A}$ be the associated Abel–Jacobi pullback defect class in $d52d^{g-1+s}(d53c^{\mathrm{ct}}_{g,n})$.

**Generation conjecture for Gorenstein kernels.** The following hold: (P1) $d6a5_{g,\mathsf A}\in\mathsf{K}_{g,n}$ for all $g$ and all $s\times n$ matrices $d538$; and (P2) the system of ideals $d4aa_{g,n}\subset\mathsf{R}^*(\mathcal{M}^{\mathrm{ct}}_{g,n})$ is the smallest system closed under properties (i)–(v) of the cited section and for which (P1) holds.

This conjecture proposes a complete geometric and structural description of the Gorenstein kernels. The stated properties are supported by the computations and known closure results, but the general assertion remains open.
quantifiers_and_scope: All g,n and all matrices, membership plus smallest ideal system closed under five properties.
individual_disposition: Properties(i)-(v) and defect classes are absent, and symbols are corrupted; cannot count complete-statement coverage. HOLD_INCOMPLETE.

title: Standard-form classification conjecture for tau-symmetric RH perturbations
exact_utf8_statement:
Let a $\tau$-symmetric Hamiltonian perturbation of the Riemann--Hopf hierarchy be written in generalized standard form, with first Hamiltonian

$$
\widetilde{H}_1=\int\left(\frac{w^3}{6}-\epsilon^2\frac{a_0}{24}w_1^2+\sum_{k\geq 4}\epsilon^k\sum_{\substack{\mu\in\mathcal{P}_k,\,l(\mu)\geq 2\\ \mu_1=\mu_2,\,m_1(\mu)=0}}\alpha_\mu w_\mu\right)dx.
$$

Here $\mathcal{P}_k$ denotes the set of partitions of $k$, $l(\mu)$ their length, $m_1(\mu)$ the multiplicity of $1$, and $w_\mu:=\prod_i w_{\mu_i}$. **Standard-form classification conjecture.** If $a_0=0$, then $\alpha_\mu=0$ for all $\mu$. If $a_0\neq0$, then $a_0,\alpha_{(2^2)},\alpha_{(2^3)},\ldots$ uniquely determine all other $\alpha_\mu$, all $\alpha_\mu$ vanish when $|\mu|$ is odd, and arbitrary values of $a_0\in\mathbb{C}^*$ and $\alpha_{(2^2)},\alpha_{(2^3)},\ldots\in\mathbb{C}$ are allowed. The supplied text gives this as a conjectural statement, with no resolution evidence.
quantifiers_and_scope: Every tau-symmetric Hamiltonian perturbation in generalized standard form, all coefficients at every order.
individual_disposition: Definitions of admissible perturbation and equivalence/generalized standard form are source-dependent; finite-order tests cannot establish existence for arbitrary infinite parameter sequences. HOLD_DEFINITIONS.
